# #2444 Three-Contract Recovery Census

## Scope and Evidence

- Governing ruling: [lead comment 5622859909](https://github.com/division-sh/swarm/issues/2444#issuecomment-5622859909), read in full. Graceful shutdown, process death, and database loss are separate contracts. No mandatory I/O timeout, universal shutdown bound, cancellation attribution, or exactly-once third-party effect promise is assumed.
- Baseline B: `/tmp/agent-g-2444-investigation`, verified HEAD `a32749a31edcf62a4c07879062c0f2e820885be6`, with the pq fork.
- Candidate C: inspected working files in `/tmp/agent-g-2444-runtime-prototype`, based on B, with stock pq and disposable owner migrations. This is an evolving shared tree, not a qualified immutable release. Other agents are changing experiment files; this report makes no claim about their unfinished experiments.
- Initial pass was read-only source/test census. The subsequently authorized F1/F2 candidate-only test probes and exact receipts are recorded below. No production fixes, provider calls, subprocess termination, or database outage were performed by this sidecar. Existing proof-ledger names remain source census unless explicitly marked as executed.
- `git diff a32749a31 --name-only` showed no changes in effects, LLM/session, runhandoff, runtime LLM/manager, startupownership, or platform spec during inspection. Within the audited fork/API families, candidate changes were the conversation transaction adapter and API SQL owner boundaries/tests. Shared PostgreSQL owner changes affect their consumers separately.

## Concrete Gaps

### F1: Fork creation has a missing durable request-to-result mapping

Exact path: `executeConversationForkCreate` passes the idempotency key only to `WithAPIIdempotency`, not to `ConversationForkCreateRequest`. `createOperatorConversationFork` inserts and commits a new `conversation_forks` row. API completion exists only in the callback return until `storeAPIIdempotency`/`storeSQLite` runs. Schema has a random primary key and nonunique source indexes, not a uniqueness fence for this request. The next lookup cannot discover the original resource by request identity.

This is a concrete memory-only association window, not loss of the fork row itself. Both process death after fork commit and an actual but unacknowledged fork COMMIT can enter it. Generic wrapper operation cancellation before its later response transaction can also leave this split outcome. The follow-on candidate HTTP handler/recorder probe now reproduces duplicate durable creation by injecting an error after real fork commit and before generic API completion, then repeating the exact keyed `conversation.fork` request. The separate SIGKILL/restart experiment remains owned elsewhere. Reuse existing idempotency completion/transaction ownership for a bounded repair; no need has been established for a new journal/framework. Selected `run.fork` also separates execution from API completion, but duplicate activation/materialization cannot be inferred without its source-freeze/admission controls.

### F2: Postcommit handoff failure erases acknowledged completion evidence

`WithCandidateHandoff` returns `handoff.Commit()` errors after the mutation function has returned success. `CandidateHandoff.Commit` can return a sink `Submit` error or work-lease `Done` error. `SettleCompletion` then returns a zero `CompletionSettlementResult` for any wrapper error; its `Committed: true` is constructed only afterward. Thus a known successful transaction followed by failed handoff is reported with false committed evidence. The same wrapper/result shape exists for SQLite.

The follow-on real selected-store probe now observes this defect on both stores with an injected `CandidateAdmission.Submit` error. The attempt is durably settled before the sink runs, the turn/spend rows exist, and the canonical run-candidate reader finds the obligation, but returned `Committed` is false. It does not establish a spontaneous production sink failure, callback/provider replay, or restart execution. C additionally has an error-only pooled transaction projection that can return cleanup error after successful COMMIT; retained SessionAuthority outcome support alone does not fix these callers. Repair must preserve true acknowledged commit evidence alongside later error; separate crash/restart proof must demonstrate actual continuation. Do not interpret false as confirmed rollback.

### F3: Migration completeness is still open

The inspected C still has direct `backend.BeginTx(ctx, ...)` in LLM session acquire/rotation/watchdog and selected-fork paths; effects authorization/response-observed transitions include manual transactions as well. Their durable readers exist, but that does not establish graceful admitted-work drain under stock pq. Treat these as explicit remaining family migrations, not a memory-recovery defect and not an excuse to introduce a universal runner. The shutdown signal must be separated from explicit operation cancellation by the owning runtime; prior operation-cancellation tests do not prove that distinction.

### F4: Named possession-proof deadline is a separate unresolved spec decision

The latest lead removes a universal mandatory I/O timeout; it does not by itself specify the replacement for these existing named owner promises:

- [platform-spec.yaml:14957](https://github.com/division-sh/swarm/blob/a32749a31edcf62a4c07879062c0f2e820885be6/platform-spec.yaml#L14957), `runtime_startup_authority_facts.possession_loss_contract.operation_error_recheck`: one independent proof before returning from the serialized process operation, bounded by the configured monitor deadline; failure/timeout terminalizes grants; an unbounded background-context recheck is forbidden.
- [platform-spec.yaml:14962](https://github.com/division-sh/swarm/blob/a32749a31edcf62a4c07879062c0f2e820885be6/platform-spec.yaml#L14962), `terminal_readback`: after physical possession is unexpectedly released, successor classification is bounded by the same deadline; incomplete/unavailable evidence must promptly yield ownership-unprovable, not leave local grants live.
- [platform-spec.yaml:36069](https://github.com/division-sh/swarm/blob/a32749a31edcf62a4c07879062c0f2e820885be6/platform-spec.yaml#L36069), `grants`: ordinary cancellation preserves healthy possession; native cancellation is armed before caller-cancellable BEGIN; failed release is decided by an independently bounded possession proof. These native-BEGIN requirements also need an explicit replacement when the custom API is removed.

C's [AdvisoryLockLease.proveCurrent](/tmp/agent-g-2444-runtime-prototype/internal/store/internal/backend/postgres/session_authority.go:846) creates `probeCtx` with the requested deadline, but passes `context.WithoutCancel(probeCtx)` to the query and checks `probeCtx.Err()` only after SQL returns. Thus this implementation does not enforce the specified proof deadline on a silent query. `processCapability` operation-error/release rechecks call this same monitor owner. This is a direct specification/implementation mismatch, independently of whether production silence has been reproduced. It must not be described as compliant merely because universal timeouts were rejected.

Consolidated decision needed: either retain and implement the existing **consumer-scoped** bounded possession-proof promise (with its own availability/healthy-silence tradeoff and exact proof), or explicitly amend these clauses to the approved replacement detection/escalation and local admission/grant policy. Do not silently extend a foreground admitted-mutation drain rule to this independent proof. `boundedTerminalResult` currently passes a timeout context to terminal readback; this census does not prove that all of its downstream blocking behavior satisfies the bound, nor that it shares the exact detached-query defect. It needs its own silence/partial-read test. No new universal timeout or transport framework is proposed.

## Database Loss and Readiness Policy

- `StartupPostgresOwner.AcquireProcessCapability` first obtains the exact shared-store advisory lease, then reads/writes durable process authority through that session. Busy remote ownership refuses startup; new local process or closed old socket is not takeover evidence. [E17]
- `processCapability` uses a 1s monitor cadence and configured 2s proof deadline by default. It serializes against current process operations before probing. C's standalone proof SQL is detached and checks deadline after drain: those numbers are **not** a promised upper bound on detecting silence. B's fork-native proof machinery differs; no universal B bound is claimed. [E18]
- Once the process capability terminalizes as ownership-unprovable/superseded, grant-dependent admission refuses; `startServeOwnershipWatch` records ownership loss and cancels serve, and `serveCancellationExitCode` returns 1. The existing idle-session termination test exercises this detected-loss path. It is not server restart, partition, or remote-work-outlives-local-close proof. [E19]
- A failed independent request/session does not automatically prove every DB connection or the process ownership lease failed. Its owner must fail/fence that operation. Global executable readiness follows actual process authority, not a blanket inference from one pooled SQL error. Whether every affected family propagates a detected failure to all appropriate readiness surfaces remains integrated proof work.
- An in-flight COMMIT error remains unproven settlement. Existing recovery facts/identities, not callback retry or inspecting the predecessor's local socket, decide continuation after DB authority is reacquired. Durable-data destruction is outside this connection-loss contract.
- No mandatory `SWARM_POSTGRES_IO_TIMEOUT`, socket wrapper, guaranteed remote lock-release timing, or hard shutdown deadline is justified by this census. Earlier test receipts that set that variable remain receipts of the earlier disposable configuration only. Timeout experiments and their removal are owned elsewhere.
- The preceding no-universal-timeout statement does not resolve F4's existing named possession-proof deadline. Silent proof/recheck/readback and exact local grant retirement remain unproven until the consolidated spec decision and proof land.

## Bottom Line

Durable recovery readers are present for effect attempts/settled responses, live-session state, run candidates, selected route truth, forkchat groups and atomic event publication. No basis was found to replace them with a new registry/outbox or to promise exactly-once external execution. F1's missing durable request association and F2's committed-evidence propagation gap are now reproduced by bounded injections on both candidate stores. Both predate fork removal in source and remain unfixed. F3 migration completeness, F4's named bounded-proof spec decision, and the three-contract composed experiments are still open. Other agents own those experiments; none is claimed complete here.
